title: Consciousness is the Self
full: caitanyam ātmā
words: neuter nominative singular abstract noun, -ya derivative of cetana
masculine nominative singular; stem ātman → nominative ātmā
proof: no overt verb: Sanskrit permits a nominal equation with understood asti
literal: Consciousness is the self.
alternatives: The self is conscious nature; awareness constitutes what is meant by Self.
judgement: The Sanskrit establishes an identification, not a Cartesian proof that any individual stream of experience owns the universe. Distinguish caitanya (consciousness) from mere citta (mental contents).
recognition: Begin with whatever is perceived; ask what knowing itself means. The sūtra points to the subject as consciousness, not to a new object to discover.
exercise: Which word is masculine, and which neuter? Does the equation require both to have the same gender?
answer: ātmā is masculine; caitanyam neuter. A Sanskrit predicate noun need not share gender with its subject.
script_focus: चै = c + ai; त = ta; न्य = n + ya; म् = final m. आत्मा begins with independent आ and uses the conjunct त्म.
why: The first line lets the student hear what Sanskrit actually identifies, rather than memorize an English metaphysical slogan.
author: Vasugupta (traditionally attributed)
source_note: 77-sūtra recension 22+10+45; source has been independently checked; differs from repo 75-count transcript.
context_devanagari: चैतन्यम् आत्मा

title: Knowledge can bind
full: jñānaṃ bandhaḥ
proof: nominal equation [asti] is understood, not written
literal: Knowledge is bondage.
alternatives: Knowing binds; a particular form of knowledge is a fetter.
judgement: Do not turn jñāna into “ignorance” to smooth the apparent contradiction. Context and commentary distinguish contracted, differentiated knowing from supreme recognition.
recognition: After 1.1 identifies consciousness with the Self, 1.2 warns that the way cognition divides the world into finite knower and object may function as bondage. Grammar shows a paradox, commentary interprets it.
exercise: Find the common nominative case in jñānam and bandhaḥ. Which English word has been added?
answer: Both are nominatives; “is” is supplied in translation as an understood copula.
script_focus: ज्ञा = ज् + ञ + ा; ं at the end of ज्ञानं is anusvāra. The भ of बन्धः is aspirated, and धः ends with visarga.
why: An apparently shocking claim becomes a lesson in gender and the interpretive danger of translating jñāna as only “wisdom.”
author: Vasugupta (traditionally attributed)
source_note: 77-sūtra recension 22+10+45; source has been independently checked; differs from repo 75-count transcript.
context_devanagari: ज्ञानं बन्धः

title: The sudden upsurge
full: udyamo bhairavaḥ
proof: udyamaḥ + bhairavaḥ → udyamo bhairavaḥ: -aḥ before voiced bh becomes -o
literal: The upsurge is Bhairava.
alternatives: The sudden rising of awareness is Bhairava; energetic emergence itself is Bhairava.
judgement: Udyama also means effort or enterprise in ordinary Sanskrit. The supreme “upsurge” reading is interpretive and must be grounded in Śaiva commentary, not declared the dictionary meaning.
recognition: Look at the instant of emergence before it is described. The sutra’s compressed claim treats this powerful uprising as the divine; it does not promise an induced energetic event.
exercise: Undo the visible -o: which word ending produced it, and why here?
answer: udyamo reflects udyamaḥ before the voiced b(h) of bhairavaḥ.
script_focus: उ = independent u; द्य is द् + य; भै = भ + ai sign; र = ra; वः = vaḥ.
why: First precise visarga-sandhi rule; profound meaning kept separate from a dictionary gloss.
author: Vasugupta (traditionally attributed)
source_note: 77-sūtra recension 22+10+45; source has been independently checked; differs from repo 75-count transcript.
context_devanagari: उद्यमो भैरवः

title: Mind, as mantra
full: cittaṃ mantraḥ
words: mind, the cognizing field, mental content
proof: cit + ta → citta is a traditional participial/derived stem (do not present this as an exhaustive Pāṇinian proof)
literal: Mind is mantra.
alternatives: The mind is a mantra; consciousness configured as mind has mantric potential.
judgement: This does not mean every distracting thought is a traditionally authorized mantra. Such an expansion would require commentary or explicit modern adaptation.
recognition: Listen to the way an utterance is known before it is spoken. This is a meditation on the inseparability of sound and cognition, not permission to invent new bīja-mantras.
exercise: Why is cittaṃ not spelled चित्तम् in this edition? Can both spellings represent a final nasal?
answer: चित्तं uses anusvāra, while चित्तम् writes explicit m with virāma; they can be equivalent in this phonological position but should not be conflated graphically.
script_focus: चित्तं: चि = ca + i sign; त्त = त् + त; ं anusvāra. मन्त्रः uses the न्त्र consonant cluster.
why: Introduces conjunct recognition and a productive warning about technical terms.
author: Vasugupta (traditionally attributed)
source_note: 77-sūtra recension 22+10+45; source has been independently checked; differs from repo 75-count transcript.
context_devanagari: चित्तं मन्त्रः

title: The teacher is a means
full: gurur upāyaḥ
words: teacher, one who dispels darkness in traditional interpretation
proof: guruḥ + upāyaḥ → gurur upāyaḥ: final -uḥ becomes -ur before vowel
literal: The teacher is the means.
alternatives: The guru is an approach; the teacher functions as a means of entry.
judgement: Do not translate guru as an infallible individual. The sūtra names a spiritual function; safeguards against abuse are separate ethical necessities.
recognition: The person who helps awareness recognize its own nature is called upāya here. A grammar book can show the equivalence; lived discernment determines how to approach teachers.
exercise: Which hidden word ending appears as r in gurur?
answer: guruḥ, nominative singular, changes to gurur before upāyaḥ.
script_focus: गु (gu) and रु (ru) have different vowel signs; उपायः opens with independent उ, while या carries long ā.
why: A compact first example of the uḥ → ur pattern, with an ethical distinction.
author: Vasugupta (traditionally attributed)
source_note: 77-sūtra recension 22+10+45; source has been independently checked; differs from repo 75-count transcript.
context_devanagari: गुरुर् उपायः

title: The body as offering
full: śarīraṃ haviḥ
proof: note the dictionary stem ends in -s, but the nominative surface has -ḥ
literal: The body is the sacrificial oblation.
alternatives: The body is an offering; embodied experience is offered in the sacrificial act.
judgement: It does not instruct the reader to injure the body. Śaiva ritual symbolism here is a different claim from literal destruction.
recognition: Imagine that a sensory experience is not a stain on spirituality but material that can be offered into awareness. The body is part of worship, not an enemy.
exercise: The lemma of haviḥ is havis, not “haviḥ” as an unchanging root. What gender are both nouns?
answer: The stem is havis; both śarīram and haviḥ are neuter nominative singulars.
script_focus: शरीरं contains long ī sign ी; हविः uses short i ि and visarga ः.
why: Ties the earlier mealtime prayer to body symbolism without repeating that prayer.
author: Vasugupta (traditionally attributed)
source_note: 77-sūtra recension 22+10+45; source has been independently checked; differs from repo 75-count transcript.
context_devanagari: शरीरं हविः

title: Conversation as recitation
full: kathā japaḥ
proof: kathā remains nominative singular with long -ā
japa + ḥ → japaḥ masculine nominative singular
literal: Conversation is recitation.
alternatives: Speech is japa; ordinary conversation can function as recitation.
judgement: Neither kathā nor japa grammatically says “all utterances are automatically sacred.” Interpret that proposition through context and awareness, not as a license to ignore the ethics of speech.
recognition: Let one ordinary sentence be spoken deliberately. This contemporary contemplative application uses the identification as a reminder that speaking need not be outside practice.
exercise: How can a feminine noun be equated with a masculine one?
answer: Predicate nouns can differ in gender; kathā is feminine and japaḥ masculine.
script_focus: कथा contains long आ as a vowel sign (था), not independent आ. जपः ends in visarga.
why: An extraordinarily memorable line that makes grammar immediately useful in daily life.
author: Vasugupta (traditionally attributed)
source_note: 77-sūtra recension 22+10+45; source has been independently checked; differs from repo 75-count transcript.
context_devanagari: कथा जपः

title: Becoming comparable to Śiva
full: śivatulyo jāyate
words: comes to be, becomes, is born
proof: śivatulyaḥ + jāyate → śivatulyo jāyate (aḥ → o before voiced j)
√jan → jāyate is a present middle form
literal: He becomes comparable to Śiva.
alternatives: One becomes Śiva-like; one comes to be equal in nature to Śiva.
judgement: Tulya states comparison/equality; it does not automatically mean a historically limited person acquires unlimited physical capacities.
recognition: The verbal form matters: this is not just a timeless equation but a predication of becoming. Let it sharpen the question: what kind of recognition does the tradition call Śiva-like?
exercise: Why is there an -o at the end of śivatulyo? Name the verb ending in jāyate.
answer: Underlying śivatulyaḥ produces -o; jāyate is 3rd singular present middle.
script_focus: शिव = śiva; तुल्य includes ल् + य; जा uses long ā; यते is ya-te.
why: Introduces finite verbs after a series of nominal aphorisms.
author: Vasugupta (traditionally attributed)
source_note: 77-sūtra recension 22+10+45; source has been independently checked; differs from repo 75-count transcript.
context_devanagari: शिवतुल्यो जायते

title: What place is not sacred?
full: sākṣādbhavanmaye nātha sarvasmin bhuvanāntare | kiṃ na bhaktimatāṃ kṣetram mantraḥ kvaiṣāṃ na siddhyati
words: neuter interrogative nominative singular, adverbially “what?” in this question
genitive plural of -mat possessive adjective used as noun
proof: bhakti + mat → bhaktimat (possessing devotion), genitive plural bhaktimatām → bhaktimatāṃ (anusvāra spelling)
the rhetorical question relies on context, not a change of noun cases
literal: What is not a sacred field for devotees?
alternatives: For people of devotion, what could fail to be a sacred place?
judgement: Kṣetra means field, domain or sacred location depending on context; the English “everywhere is a temple” is an interpretation, not the word-by-word reading.
recognition: The full verse speaks of a universe filled directly by the Lord. The rhetorical question changes how ordinary places are understood without requiring special scenery.
exercise: What does the -mat suffix contribute to bhaktimat, and why is -ām plural?
answer: It means possessing bhakti; bhaktimatāṃ is genitive plural, “of devotees.”
script_focus: भक्तिमतां: भ + क् + ति + म + तां. क्षेत्रम्: क्ष = क् + ष; त्र = त् + र; final म् explicit.
why: Moves beyond equations into a sentence whose answer depends on grammatical negation and rhetoric.
author: Utpaladeva
source_note: Mahānaya + GRETIL Bailly text; individual readings require final comparison with Kṣemarāja commentary.
context_devanagari: साक्षाद्भवन्मये नाथ सर्वस्मिन् भुवनान्तरे । किं न भक्तिमतां क्षेत्रम् मन्त्रः क्वैषां न सिद्ध्यति ॥

title: You alone are the Self
full: tvam evātmeśa sarvasya sarvaś cātmani rāgavān | iti svabhāvasiddhāṃs tvadbhaktiṃ jānañ jayej janaḥ
proof: tvam + eva → tvam eva (m before vowel retained in this segmentation)
ātmā + īśa → ātmeśa (ā + ī → e, guṇa)
the input phrase tvam evātmeśa encodes two successive boundaries
literal: You alone are the Self of all, O Lord.
alternatives: You yourself, Lord, are the self belonging to everything.
judgement: Here īśa is a vocative, not part of a new lexical compound “ātmeśa” meaning only “lord of the self.” The adjacent Sanskrit of the whole verse controls how the fusion is understood.
recognition: The poet addresses someone as “you” and identifies that addressee with the Self of all. His devotion uses second-person language to express a nondual claim, rather than cancelling relationship.
exercise: Undo evātmeśa into its elements and identify the two vowel meetings.
answer: eva + ātmā + īśa; a+ā→ā and ā+ī→e.
script_focus: त्वम् has a final consonant; एव has independent ए; आत्मा opens with आ; ईश contains independent ई; सर्वस्य has the स्य conjunct.
why: First multiple-step sandhi chain: the point is that syntax must come before a seductive compound gloss.
author: Utpaladeva
source_note: Mahānaya + GRETIL Bailly text; individual readings require final comparison with Kṣemarāja commentary.
context_devanagari: त्वम् एवात्मेश सर्वस्य सर्वश् चात्मनि रागवान् । इति स्वभावसिद्धांस् त्वद्भक्तिं जानञ् जयेज् जनः ॥

title: Śiva at play with Śakti
full: eṣa devo 'nayā devyā nityaṃ krīḍārasotsukaḥ | vicitrān sṛṣṭisaṃhārān vidhatte yugapad vibhuḥ
words: eager for the flavour of play
proof: eṣaḥ + devaḥ → eṣa devo (visarga before voiced d gives o)
devaḥ + anayā → devo ’nayā (-aḥ + a gives -o with elided a)
literal: This god, with this goddess, is always eager for the relish of play.
alternatives: The Lord, together with Śakti, perpetually delights in the taste of play.
judgement: Krīḍā is play, rasa is flavour/savour, utsuka is eager or desirous. “Cosmic consciousness must be perpetually blissful in a clinical sense” does not follow from these lexical meanings.
recognition: The line is a description, not an instruction to feel exhilarated. It invites the reader to consider whether manifestation can be conceived as an expression of freedom rather than an external task imposed on God.
exercise: Why does devī appear as devyā, and which word tells you this refers to “this goddess”?
answer: devyā is feminine instrumental singular; anayā is the matching feminine demonstrative instrumental.
script_focus: देव्या has द + े, व् + य + ा; क्रीडा has conjunct क्र; रसोत्सुक has अ + उ → ओ in compound sandhi.
why: Introduces instrumental agreement in a theologically vivid sentence.
author: Abhinavagupta
source_note: Mahānaya + GRETIL transcription; punctuation, compounds and variant vowels still require printed-witness rights check.
context_devanagari: एष देवोऽनया देव्या नित्यं क्रीडारसोत्सुकः । विचित्रान् सृष्टिसंहारान् विधत्ते युगपद् विभुः ॥

title: He makes creation and withdrawal
full: eṣa devo 'nayā devyā nityaṃ krīḍārasotsukaḥ | vicitrān sṛṣṭisaṃhārān vidhatte yugapad vibhuḥ
words: creations and dissolutions / manifestations and reabsorptions
proof: vi + √dhā gives vidhatte in middle voice (do not derive by mere external sandhi)
literal: The all-pervading one simultaneously brings about varied creations and reabsorptions.
alternatives: The omnipresent Lord fashions manifold unfoldings and withdrawals all at once.
judgement: Sṛṣṭi/saṃhāra are paired cosmological actions; a literal reading does not require an astronomical claim that historical universes physically appear simultaneously.
recognition: After 11’s “play” this line gives its verbs and objects. The grammar makes clear what he does (accusative plural), how (yugapad), and who does it (vibhuḥ).
exercise: Identify the agent, direct object and adverb. What distinguishes vicitrān from vibhuḥ?
answer: vibhuḥ is nom.sg agent; sṛṣṭisaṃhārān with vicitrān is acc.pl object; yugapad is indeclinable.
script_focus: सृष्टि has vocalic ṛ sign ृ and conjunct ष्ट; संहार uses anusvāra; वि-ध-त्ते contains त्त.
why: First nontrivial full verbal sentence: agreement and object marking become unmistakable.

title: The goddess longs to recognise herself
full: tasyaivaiṣā parā devī svarūpāmarśanotsukā | pūrṇatvaṃ sarvabhaveṣu yasyā nālpaṃ na cādhikam
words: genitive masculine/neuter singular demonstrative + emphatic particle
eager to apprehend/reflect upon her own nature
proof: tasyaiva + eṣā → tasyaivaiṣā (a + e → ai across next boundary)
literal: This is the supreme goddess of that very one, eager to apprehend her own nature.
alternatives: His supreme power is this goddess, intent upon her own self-awareness.
judgement: Āmarśana means reflective apprehension, contact or deliberation; rendering it as “self-reflexive consciousness” is legitimate philosophical explanation but not a one-word dictionary translation.
recognition: Trika often pairs prakāśa (illumination) and vimarśa (self-apprehension). The feminine nominatives show that the goddess is the grammatical subject, not a passive instrument.
exercise: Find three feminine nominative endings. How many vowel contractions hide in tasyaivaiṣā?
answer: eṣā, parā, devī and the compound ending -utsukā are feminine nominatives; tasya+eva and tasyaiva+eṣā have two contractions.
script_focus: तस्यै = त + स्य + ै; एषा begins with ए; आमर्शन is an ā-initial word embedded in a compound; त्सु is त् + सु.
why: A grammatical doorway into the heart of Śiva–Śakti metaphysics without collapsing translation into doctrine.
author: Abhinavagupta

title: Nothing too small or too great
quote: pūrṇatvaṃ sarvabhaveṣu yasyā nālpaṃ na cādhikam
full: tasyaivaiṣā parā devī svarūpāmarśanotsukā | pūrṇatvaṃ sarvabhaveṣu yasyā nālpaṃ na cādhikam
proof: yasyāḥ + na → yasyā na (visarga before voiced nasal disappears)
literal: Her fullness in all forms of becoming is neither deficient nor excessive.
alternatives: In everything that comes into being, her fullness admits neither too little nor too much.
judgement: Bhava has short a in the printed reading sarvabhaveṣu. Do not silently change it to bhāveṣu, even if English “states” is attractive. The line is dependent on the preceding reference to devī.
recognition: One can contemplate fullness without treating it as proof that individual suffering, scarcity or injustice are unreal. The text describes an ultimate power; it does not erase empirical differences.
exercise: Underline the two examples of a+a→ā and identify yasyā as what case.
answer: nālpam and cādhikam; yasyā is feminine genitive singular yasyāḥ before na.
script_focus: पूर्ण uses ṇ (retroflex), not dental न. भावे versus भवे matters: long ा changes lexical identity.
why: A lesson in how tiny vowels change meanings and in the ethical limits of metaphysical language.

title: A definition of inertness
full: paricchinnaprakāśatvaṃ jaḍasya kila lakṣaṇam | jaḍād vilakṣaṇo bodho yato na parimīyate
proof: pari-√chid (“cut around”) yields paricchinna, a past participial adjective “delimited”
literal: Limited manifestation is, indeed, the characteristic of what is inert.
alternatives: The mark of inertness, he says, is circumscribed disclosure.
judgement: Prakāśa can be physical light, appearance or self-disclosure. Translating every instance as “consciousness” before the argument develops would beg the question.
recognition: Abhinavagupta sets up a contrast, not an empirical test of neural correlates. Read the next lesson before concluding what he intends by the word jaḍa.
exercise: What grammatical ending makes “limited manifestation” an abstract property rather than a finite verb?
answer: -tva, in paricchinnaprakāśatvam. The genitive jaḍasya supplies “of the inert.”
script_focus: परिच्छिन्न includes च्छ and न्न conjuncts. प्रकाश has प्र = प् + र; जड uses ड, not द.
why: Theory enters as an explicit definition; learners see why technical nouns cannot be translated lazily.

title: Why awareness differs
quote: jaḍād vilakṣaṇo bodho yato na parimīyate
full: paricchinnaprakāśatvaṃ jaḍasya kila lakṣaṇam | jaḍād vilakṣaṇo bodho yato na parimīyate
proof: jaḍāt + vilakṣaṇaḥ → jaḍād vilakṣaṇaḥ (t→d before voiced v)
literal: Awareness differs from the inert, because it is not measurable or bounded.
alternatives: Conscious apprehension is distinguished from inert things precisely in not being circumscribable.
judgement: Na parimīyate is not a scientific theorem that awareness can never be quantified by any operational metric. The verse asserts a philosophical distinction concerning self-disclosure.
recognition: The paired 8a/8b becomes a miniature argument: first a proposed distinguishing mark, then the contrast. The ablative jaḍāt is crucial to its structure.
exercise: Which two nominatives agree? Why does jaḍād end in d even though the underlying case ending is -āt?
answer: bodhaḥ with vilakṣaṇaḥ; final t voices to d before the voiced v.
script_focus: जडात् is ablative; जडाद् is its voiced sandhi outcome. मीय in परिमीयते writes long ī.
why: Our first explicit premise-and-contrast argument, with three exact consonant/visarga transformations.

title: Even not-knowing is named
full: yad etasyāparijñānaṃ tatsvātantryaṃ hi varṇitam | sa eva khalu saṃsāro mūḍānāṃ yo vibhīṣakaḥ
words: neuter nominative singular past passive participle
proof: tat + svātantryam → tatsvātantryam (t+s remains ts sequence)
svatantra → svātantrya is a lexical derivative with vowel gradation, not ordinary external sandhi
literal: What is non-recognition of this one has indeed been described as that very freedom.
alternatives: Even the failure to recognise him is spoken of as an exercise of his sovereignty.
judgement: This is one of the most easily mishandled statements: the metaphysical inclusion of ignorance under divine freedom is not the practical claim that ignorance is desirable or harmless.
recognition: The relative–correlative yad ... tat is a Sanskrit argumentative structure. It says something startling, but only after you parse what “that” refers to.
exercise: Identify the two halves of the relative/correlative construction. What does the prefix a- negate?
answer: yat ... tat; a- negates parijñāna, making “non-recognition.”
script_focus: अपरिज्ञान has an initial privative अ; स्वतन्त्र्य contains त्र्य = त् + र् + य; वर्णितम् contains retroflex ण.
why: Introduces relative pronouns and avoids the mystic shorthand “ignorance is freedom” without qualifiers.
author: Abhinavagupta
source_note: Mahānaya + GRETIL transcription; punctuation, compounds and variant vowels still require printed-witness rights check.

title: The grammar of liberation
quote: yat tattvasya parijñānaṃ sa mokṣaḥ parameśataḥ
full: yat tattvasya parijñānaṃ sa mokṣaḥ parameśataḥ | tat pūrṇatvaṃ prabuddhānāṃ jīvanmuktiś ca sā smṛtā
words: from / on account of the Supreme Lord
proof: saḥ + mokṣaḥ → sa mokṣaḥ (before nasal m)
parameśa + -tas → parameśataḥ, source or standpoint depending on construal
literal: Complete understanding of reality—this is liberation, through the Supreme Lord.
alternatives: What is recognition of the real is precisely what the text calls liberation.
judgement: Note the change of gender: yat/parijñānam are neuter; saḥ/mokṣaḥ masculine. The anaphor can agree with its predicate noun while referring back to a neuter event. Do not invent a separate “he” who is liberated.
recognition: This supplies the natural answer to lesson 17: ignorance and recognition are not simply feelings to arrange; the text gives a definition of liberation in terms of knowing.
exercise: Why are yat and sa not the same grammatical gender? What form means “of truth”?
answer: yat relates to neuter parijñānam; saḥ is masculine with mokṣaḥ; tattvasya is genitive singular.
script_focus: तत्त्व is त + त्त्व; मोक्ष includes क्ष = क् + ष; परिज्ञान has ज्ञ.
why: A line that lets the student deduce “liberation” from Sanskrit syntax without relying on an English subtitle.
author: Abhinavagupta
source_note: Mahānaya + GRETIL transcription; punctuation, compounds and variant vowels still require printed-witness rights check.
selected_devanagari: यत् तत्त्वस्य परिज्ञानं स मोक्षः परमेशतः
context_devanagari: यत् तत्त्वस्य परिज्ञानं स मोक्षः परमेशतः । तत् पूर्णत्वं प्रबुद्धानां जीवन्मुक्तिश् च सा स्मृता ॥

title: The bound experiencer is Śiva
quote: bhoktā ca tatra dehī śiva eva gṛhītapaśubhāvaḥ
full: tatrāntar viśvam idaṃ vicitratanukaraṇabhuvanasaṃtānam | bhoktā ca tatra dehī śiva eva gṛhītapaśubhāvaḥ
words: having assumed the condition of a bound being
proof: śivaḥ + eva → śiva eva (aḥ + vowel e
visarga is dropped in this environment)
gṛhīta (from √grah) + paśu + bhāva creates a compound ending -aḥ
literal: And the embodied experiencer there is Śiva himself, having taken on the state of a bound subject.
alternatives: The one who experiences the world in a body is none other than Śiva appearing in the condition of a limited being.
judgement: Paśu in this Śaiva technical context means the bound individual; translating it as simply “animal” misses the doctrinal contrast to pati (Lord). The compound describes an adopted condition, not proof of an independently existing second entity.
recognition: The accusative and nominative machinery of the previous lessons now culminates in an identification: an embodied agent is grammatically re-described as Śiva. This is an ontological interpretation, not a denial that individual choices have consequences.
exercise: What dictionary stems produce bhoktā and dehī? Why are these not feminine long-ā/-ī words?
answer: bhoktṛ and dehin; both are masculine nominative singular with stem-specific endings.
script_focus: भोक्ता has long ā at the end but masculine nominative; देही has long ī and is likewise masculine. Script shape alone does not assign gender.
why: The deep claim of Śaiva nonduality can now be reconstructed from morphology rather than a convenient English translation.
author: Abhinavagupta

context_devanagari: तत्रान्तर् विश्वम् इदं विचित्रतनुकरणभुवनसंतानम् । भोक्ता च तत्र देही शिव एव गृहीतपशुभावः ॥

title: The spotless crystal takes colours
full: nānāvidhavarṇānāṃ rūpaṃ dhatte yathāmalaḥ sphaṭikaḥ | suramānuṣapaśupādaparūpatvaṃ tadvad īśo ’pi
words: of many kinds of colours / appearances
proof: nānā + vidha + varṇa → nānāvidhavarṇa, genitive plural -ānām
dhatte is a conjugated verb (√dhā), not a sandhi of “dhat” with “te”
literal: A spotless crystal takes on the appearance of various colours.
alternatives: Just as a clear crystal presents the forms of many colours without itself becoming their pigments.
judgement: A literal translation says the crystal “assumes form,” not that light physics has proved a metaphysical doctrine. The next pāda applies the comparison to the Lord taking divine, human and other forms.
recognition: This image is a controlled analogy: the variety of appearances does not establish a permanent plurality of separate essences. But the analogy should not flatten the real experience of difference.
exercise: Identify the object of dhatte and the noun that is its subject.
answer: rūpam is acc.sg object; sphaṭikaḥ is nom.sg subject; amalaḥ agrees with sphaṭikaḥ.
script_focus: स्फ = स् + फ; टि uses a short i sign that appears visually to the left; यथामलः contains contraction of final ā + initial a.
why: A visual analogy trains the reader to infer grammatical roles before importing philosophical theory.
author: Abhinavagupta
source_note: GRETIL transliteration checked against SanskritDocuments where appropriate; commercial reuse of GRETIL transcription not cleared.
context_devanagari: नानाविधवर्णानां रूपं धत्ते यथामलः स्फटिकः । सुरमानुषपशुपादपरूपत्वं तद्वद् ईशोऽपि ॥

title: The mirror of the intellect
full: rāhur adṛśyo 'pi yathā śaśibimbasthaḥ prakāśate tadvat | sarvagato 'py ayam ātmā viṣayāśrayaṇena dhīmukure
words: in the mirror of the intellect
proof: sarvagataḥ + api + ayam → sarvagato ’py ayam (aḥ+a → o plus avagraha
literal: This Self, although present everywhere, [appears] in the mirror of intellect through dependence on objects.
alternatives: The all-pervading Self becomes manifest in the intellect’s mirror as it takes objects for support.
judgement: The word “appears” is **supplied from prakāśate in the first half of the complete verse**; it is not a finite verb written in this excerpt. A translation must openly mark such elliptical syntax.
recognition: An image of Rāhu appearing when connected with the moon precedes this line. The point concerns manifestness, not a literal claim about an invisible astronomical body inhabiting consciousness.
exercise: Where does the English verb “appears” come from, and what case is dhīmukure?
answer: From prakāśate in the first half of the verse; dhīmukure is locative singular.
script_focus: सर्वगतोऽप्ययम्: अवग्रह ऽ indicates an elided vowel; धी has long ī; मुकुरे locative e.
why: An expert skill: recover a verb from its earlier comparative clause rather than hallucinating one into the selected phrase.
author: Abhinavagupta
source_note: GRETIL transliteration checked against SanskritDocuments where appropriate; commercial reuse of GRETIL transcription not cleared.
context_devanagari: राहुर् अदृश्योऽपि यथा शशिबिम्बस्थः प्रकाशते तद्वत् । सर्वगतोऽप्य् अयम् आत्मा विषयाश्रयणेन धीमुकुरे ॥

title: When intelligence becomes clear
full: ādarśe malarahite yadvad vadanaṃ vibhāti tadvad ayam | śivaśaktipātavimale dhītattve bhāti bhārūpaḥ
words: made clear by the descent of Śiva’s power
light-formed, of the nature of luminosity
proof: śiva + śaktipāta makes “Śiva’s grace/descent of power”
literal: In the principle of intellect purified by the descent of Śiva’s power, the luminous one shines.
alternatives: Where the intellect is clear through Śiva’s śaktipāta, the Self appears as light itself.
judgement: The masculine subject “the luminous one” is linked to ayam ātmā in the surrounding passage. “Light” is a metaphor for self-disclosure, not a prediction of visible photic phenomena.
recognition: The two locatives describe the place or cognitive condition of appearance. The poem does not assert that one should strain to produce a light vision.
exercise: Which two words are locative singular? What tense is bhāti?
answer: śivaśaktipātavimale and dhītattve; bhāti is third-person singular present active.
script_focus: शक्तिपात has क्ति conjunct and long ā in पात; धी long ī; भाति has long ā.
why: Explains how context supplies a subject across verses and resists experiential sensationalism.
author: Abhinavagupta
source_note: GRETIL transliteration checked against SanskritDocuments where appropriate; commercial reuse of GRETIL transcription not cleared.
context_devanagari: आदर्शे मलरहिते यद्वद् वदनं विभाति तद्वद् अयम् । शिवशक्तिपातविमले धीतत्त्वे भाति भारूपः ॥

title: The thirty-sixfold world appears
quote: yat paratattvaṃ tasmin vibhāti ṣaṭtriṃśadātma jagat
full: sarvavikalpavihīnaṃ śuddhaṃ śāntaṃ layodayavihīnam | yat paratattvaṃ tasmin vibhāti ṣaṭtriṃśadātma jagat
proof: ṣaṭ + triṃśat = thirty-six, then + ātman as compound-final
“ṣaṭtriṃśadātma” is an inflected compound form, not a free-standing word for “tattvas”
literal: The world, whose nature is thirty-sixfold, shines in that supreme reality.
alternatives: Within the supreme principle, the universe appears as a thirty-sixfold articulation.
judgement: The whole verse first describes that reality as free from alternatives and arising/ceasing. “Thirty-six tattvas” is a very plausible Trika contextual gloss, but the phrase literally means “thirty-six-natured.”
recognition: Syntax gives a containment claim: the thirty-sixfold world appears *in that* (tasmin), not as an independent realm outside it. This is one of the most powerful reversals of the sense of separation.
exercise: Identify the nominative subject of vibhāti and the locative in which it occurs.
answer: jagat is neuter nominative singular subject; tasmin is locative singular; ṣaṭtriṃśadātma qualifies jagat.
script_focus: षट् = ṣaṭ with final dental? ट retroflex; त्रिंशत् = triṃśat; the visible त्म cluster in आत्मा recurs inside षट्त्रिंशदात्म.
why: Case grammar here *is* metaphysical structure: in what does the world appear?
author: Abhinavagupta
source_note: GRETIL transliteration checked against SanskritDocuments where appropriate; commercial reuse of GRETIL transcription not cleared.
selected_devanagari: यत् परतत्त्वं तस्मिन् विभाति षट्त्रिंशदात्म जगत्
context_devanagari: सर्वविकल्पविहीनं शुद्धं शान्तं लयोदयविहीनम् । यत् परतत्त्वं तस्मिन् विभाति षट्त्रिंशदात्म जगत् ॥

title: The impossible made possible
full: paramaṃ yat svātantryaṃ durghaṭasaṃpādanaṃ maheśasya | devī māyāśaktiḥ svātmāvaraṇaṃ śivasya
words: bringing about what is hard/impossible to bring about
proof: dur- + ghaṭa yields durghaṭa (hard to effect)
mahat/mahā + īśa produces maheśa as a standard compound
literal: Which supreme freedom of the Great Lord accomplishes what is difficult to accomplish…
alternatives: The Lord’s sovereignty, capable of bringing the apparently impossible into manifestation, is the subject of this definition.
judgement: This selected first half is not a complete assertion: the following half identifies the goddess Māyā-śakti and the Self’s self-veiling. The punctuation must preserve that dependency.
recognition: Abhinavagupta is not promising miracles on demand. The point is that ultimate freedom can manifest limitation without becoming a second, independent principle.
exercise: What is the genitive here? Does the selected half contain a finite verb?
answer: maheśasya is genitive singular. The half-verse lacks a finite verb; its sentence continues.
script_focus: दुर्घट has र्घ conjunct; सम्पादन uses म्प; स्वतन्त्र्य and महेशस्य have multiple conjunct patterns.
why: An advanced lesson in respecting an unfinished Sanskrit clause even when it would make a wonderful standalone slogan.
author: Abhinavagupta
source_note: GRETIL transliteration checked against SanskritDocuments where appropriate; commercial reuse of GRETIL transcription not cleared.
context_devanagari: परमं यत् स्वातन्त्र्यं दुर्घटसंपादनं महेशस्य । देवी मायाशक्तिः स्वात्मावरणं शिवस्य ॥

title: Without a second, yet with You
quote: advitīyā api sadā tvaddvitīyā api prabho
full: jayanti bhaktipīyūṣarasāsavavaronmadāḥ | advitīyā api sadā tvaddvitīyā api prabho
proof: a- + dvitīya → advitīya (not possessing a second)
advitīyāḥ + api → advitīyā api (visarga of masculine āḥ is lost before initial a)
tvad + dvitīya makes tvaddvitīya with assimilated consonant cluster
literal: Though without a second, they always have You as their second, O Lord.
alternatives: Even in nonduality, devotees remain in relationship to You.
judgement: The apparent contradiction is deliberately poetic. Advitīya is not simply “lonely”; tvaddvitīya is a relational compound, not a literal assertion that reality has become numerically two.
recognition: Utpaladeva keeps both the address to the Lord and the recognition of nonduality. In a living devotional idiom, relation need not mean separation: the second person survives as a form of intimacy.
exercise: Which endings are masculine nominative plural, and what does the prefix a- negate?
answer: advitīyāḥ and tvaddvitīyāḥ, with visarga dropped in the surface; a- negates the idea of a “second.”
script_focus: द्वि includes द् + व; ती has long ī; तीयाः masculine plural becomes तिया before api under sandhi; प्रभो has long o.
why: An unforgettable compound paradox whose grammar prevents a superficial “nonduality means no love” conclusion.
author: Utpaladeva

selected_devanagari: अद्वितीया अपि सदा त्वद्द्वितीया अपि प्रभो
context_devanagari: जयन्ति भक्तिपीयूषरसासववरोन्मदाः । अद्वितीया अपि सदा त्वद्द्वितीया अपि प्रभो ॥

title: Two identical sounds, two different pronouns
quote: anantānandasindhos te nātha tattvaṃ vidanti te
full: anantānandasindhos te nātha tattvaṃ vidanti te | tādṛśa eva ye sāndrabhaktyānandarasāplutāḥ
words: of the ocean of endless bliss
proof: sindhoḥ + te → sindhos te (visarga before dental t becomes s)
te¹ and te² share spelling but come from different pronouns
literal: They know your reality, O Lord, of you who are an ocean of infinite bliss.
alternatives: Those immersed in the bliss of devotion know what You truly are, O Lord.
judgement: The two te forms **do not** mean the same thing. First “your,” second “they.” The following relative ye... identifies who “they” are. A sentence translation without that context is structurally incomplete.
recognition: This is the exact point of the book: the student sees identical phonetic strings, discovers distinct morphological functions and stops trusting an English line alone.
exercise: Label te¹ and te². Which one is “your”? What is the finite verb?
answer: te¹ is gen.sg of the second person; te² nominative plural demonstrative; vidanti is 3pl present.
script_focus: अनन्तानन्द contains two long ā vowels; सिन्धोः ends with visarga; वेद? Here the actual verb is विदन्ति with short i.
why: The best demonstration in the entire volume of why case, not intuition, determines meaning.
author: Utpaladeva
source_note: Mahānaya + GRETIL Bailly text; individual readings require final comparison with Kṣemarāja commentary.
context_devanagari: अनन्तानन्दसिन्धोस्ते नाथ तत्त्वं विदन्ति ते । तादृश एव ये सान्द्रभक्त्यानन्दरसाप्लुताः ॥

title: Visible amid the turmoil of knowing
full: nātha vedyakṣaye kena na dṛśyo 'sy ekakaḥ sthitaḥ | vedyavedakasaṃkṣobhe 'py asi bhaktaiḥ sudarśanaḥ
words: amid the agitation of known and knower
proof: vedya (what is to be known) + vedaka (knower) + saṃkṣobha → compound with -e locative
saṃkṣobhe + api + asi → saṃkṣobhe ’py asi (a of api elided after e, i becomes y before a)
literal: Even amid the turbulence of known and knower, you are readily seen by devotees.
alternatives: To devotees, You remain visible even where knowing and its object seem locked in agitation.
judgement: Sudārśana should not be printed: the source gives sudarśana (short a). The “devotee sees” assertion is theological; it does not mandate ocular visions.
recognition: The perceiver–perceived distinction is not erased by refusing to notice objects. The devotional gaze understands the play of cognition as the arena of disclosure.
exercise: Why is bhaktaiḥ instrumental plural rather than nominative? How is the apostrophe formed?
answer: -aiḥ marks instrumental plural, “by devotees.” The avagraha marks a lost a from api after -e, while i changes to y before asi.
script_focus: वे द्य has द् + य; संक्षोभे contains क्ष; भक्तैः has diphthong ai and visarga.
why: An advanced but rewarding demonstration of multiple sandhis and agentive instrumentals.
author: Utpaladeva
source_note: Mahānaya + GRETIL Bailly text; individual readings require final comparison with Kṣemarāja commentary.
context_devanagari: नाथ वेद्यक्षये केन न दृश्योऽस्य् एककः स्थितः । वेद्यवेदकसंक्षोभेऽप्यसि भक्तैः सुदर्शनः ॥

title: May devotion never be separated
quote: aviyuktāsti te tadvad ekā tvadbhaktir astu me
full: anantānandasarasī devī priyatamā yathā | aviyuktāsti te tadvad ekā tvadbhaktir astu me
proof: bhaktiḥ + astu → bhaktir astu (iḥ before vowel becomes ir)
√as present asti versus imperative astu differ in final vowel
literal: Just so, may my single devotion to You exist, as [Your goddess] is inseparable from You.
alternatives: May devotion to You be as inseparable from me as Your beloved goddess is from You.
judgement: The first half of the verse gives the Goddess as the simile; without it, aviyuktā appears without an overtly stated feminine subject. Keep the full stanza visible.
recognition: An explicit prayer enters late in the curriculum. The reader can distinguish statement asti (“is”) from wish astu (“let it be”). The devotional request is not a logical denial of separation; it is a lived petition.
exercise: Find two forms of √as. Which is a fact claim and which a wish?
answer: asti is present indicative 3rd singular; astu is imperative 3rd singular.
script_focus: अस्ति and अस्तु differ by one vowel sign; भक्तिरस्तु writes r from भक्ति: + अस्तु sandhi.
why: A finely shaped lesson in verbal mood, complete-verse context and the meaning of a devotional wish.
author: Utpaladeva
source_note: Mahānaya + GRETIL Bailly text; individual readings require final comparison with Kṣemarāja commentary.
selected_devanagari: अवियुक्तास्ति ते तद्वद् एका त्वद्भक्तिर् अस्तु मे
context_devanagari: अनन्तानन्दसरसी देवी प्रियतमा यथा । अवियुक्तास्ति ते तद्वद् एका त्वद्भक्तिर् अस्तु मे ॥

title: Three flavours of the path
full: sarva eva bhavallābhahetur bhaktimatāṃ vibho | saṃvinmārgo ’yam āhlādaduḥkhamohais tridhā sthitaḥ
proof: mārga + ḥ before ayam → mārgo ’yam (aḥ+a yields o and avagraha)
āhlāda + duḥkha + moha produces a coordinated compound, instrumental plural -aiḥ
the internal -n- in saṃvinmārga must be checked against the chosen witness rather than “proven” by a made-up sandhi rule
literal: This path of awareness is established threefold through delight, suffering and delusion.
alternatives: For devotees, the path of consciousness is lived in three registers: joy, distress and bewilderment.
judgement: Tridhā means “threefold”; the Sanskrit does not say that all three emotional modes are equivalently pleasant, or that pain must be rebranded as bliss.
recognition: Utpaladeva places ordinary emotional life within the path rather than requiring its replacement. The grammatical instrumental plural makes the three modes part of the manner or conditions of the path.
exercise: Which form expresses the three manners, and why is tridhā not a feminine singular noun?
answer: āhlādaduḥkhamohaiḥ is instrumental plural; tridhā is an indeclinable adverb.
script_focus: संविन् + मार्ग is an internal compound; the अवग्रह in मार्गोऽयम् marks the following initial a.
why: Bridges the emotional prayer book with philological care about emotion and religious meaning.
author: Utpaladeva
source_note: Mahānaya + GRETIL Bailly text; individual readings require final comparison with Kṣemarāja commentary.
context_devanagari: सर्व एव भवल्लाभहेतुर् भक्तिमतां विभो । संविन्मार्गोऽयम् आह्लाददुःखमोहैस् त्रिधा स्थितः ॥

title: Devotion becomes a science
full: bhavadbhaktimahāvidyā yeṣām abhyāsam āgatā | vidyāvidyobhayasyāpi tā ete tattvavedinaḥ
words: great knowledge / wisdom of devotion to you
proof: bhavat + bhakti yields bhavad-bhakti through voicing of final t before voiced bh
abhi + √as yields abhyāsa as lexical noun (do not pretend this is ordinary a+a sandhi)
āgatā feminine nominative agrees with vidyā
literal: Those into whose practice the great science of devotion to You has come…
alternatives: People whose ongoing discipline has been entered by the great knowledge of devotion to You…
judgement: A complete translation requires the next half-verse: these are knowers of the reality of both knowledge and ignorance. The first half is an unfinished relative clause.
recognition: Here the book teaches restraint. We can love a resonant half-line while admitting that the syntax needs its continuation. Devotion is treated as a vidyā, a disciplined knowing, not mere intensity of feeling.
exercise: What word does āgatā agree with? Why does yeṣām not mean “who” as a nominative?
answer: It agrees with feminine mahāvidyā; yeṣām is genitive plural “of whom.”
script_focus: विद्या includes द् + य; अभ्यास has भ्य; आगता begins with independent long आ.
why: Makes the reader more faithful to poetry by refusing to stop a Sanskrit relative clause prematurely.
author: Utpaladeva
source_note: Mahānaya + GRETIL Bailly text; individual readings require final comparison with Kṣemarāja commentary.
context_devanagari: भवद्भक्तिमहाविद्या येषाम् अभ्यासम् आगता । विद्याविद्योभयस्यापि ता एते तत्त्ववेदिनः ॥

title: The “I” that feels happy and sad
quote: ahaṃ sukhī ca duḥkhī ca raktaś cetyādisaṃvidaḥ
full: ahaṃ sukhī ca duḥkhī ca raktaś cetyādisaṃvidaḥ | sukhādyavasthānusyūte vartante ’nyatra tāḥ sphuṭam
proof: raktaḥ + ca → raktaś ca (visarga becomes ś before palatal c)
saṃvid feminine nominative plural is saṃvidaḥ, not a masculine singular ending
literal: Experiences such as “I am happy, I am sad, I am attached”…
alternatives: The cognitions “I am happy,” “I am distressed,” “I am in love,” and the like…
judgement: This is a plural **subject phrase**, not a standalone assertion about what the “I” essentially is. The next half says these cognitions appear in another principle through the succession of states.
recognition: Notice that happiness and sadness are first introduced as predications (“I am ...”), then reclassified as cognitions. The syntax begins the inquiry into what persists across changing mental states.
exercise: What is feminine plural here, and which two long-ī forms are masculine nominatives?
answer: saṃvidaḥ is feminine nom.pl; sukhī and duḥkhī are masculine nom.sg of -in stems.
script_focus: रक्तश्चे: रक् + त, then च्; चेत्य writes त्य. सुखी and दुःखी both long ी.
why: A practical demonstration of the difference between the content of a self-description and the knowing of that content.
author: Kallaṭa / Vasugupta tradition; exact authorship debated
source_note: GRETIL + Mahānaya; do not assert sole authorship with certainty.
selected_devanagari: अहं सुखी च दुःखी च रक्तश्चेत्यादिसंविदः
context_devanagari: अहं सुखी च दुःखी च रक्तश्चेत्यादिसंविदः । सुखाद्यवस्थानुस्यूते वर्तन्तेऽन्यत्र ताः स्फुटम् ॥

title: Beyond the polarity of pleasure and pain
quote: na duḥkhaṃ na sukhaṃ yatra na grāhyaṃ grāhakaṃ na ca
full: na duḥkhaṃ na sukhaṃ yatra na grāhyaṃ grāhakaṃ na ca | na cāsti mūḍhabhāvo ’pi tad asti paramārthataḥ
words: neuter nominative singular in this contrast
proof: the second half supplies asti (“exists”), absent in the selected first half
literal: Where there is neither pain nor pleasure, neither object nor subject…
alternatives: Where pleasure and pain, what is grasped and what grasps, no longer divide the field…
judgement: The negations concern ultimate analysis and do not entail bodily anaesthesia or an inability to distinguish ordinary subjects and objects. The first half is grammatically completed by the second.
recognition: The paired participial forms grāhya and grāhaka allow the reader to feel a philosophical contrast in suffixes: to-be-known versus knower. The theological reading must be downstream of that morphology.
exercise: Why are grāhya and grāhaka not the same word? Which verb is supplied in the second half?
answer: -ya produces the potential/passive sense and -aka an agentive sense; asti appears in the second half.
script_focus: ग्राह्यम्: ह्य = ह् + य; ग्राहकं uses क instead. दुःखं contains visarga-like sign inside word and anusvāra at end.
why: The argument deepens: ultimate nonduality is not the suppression of experience but questioning its presumed segmentation.
author: Kallaṭa / Vasugupta tradition; exact authorship debated
source_note: GRETIL + Mahānaya; do not assert sole authorship with certainty.
selected_devanagari: न दुःखं न सुखं यत्र न ग्राह्यं ग्राहकं न च
context_devanagari: न दुःखं न सुखं यत्र न ग्राह्यं ग्राहकं न च । न चास्ति मूढभावोऽपि तद् अस्ति परमार्थतः ॥

title: Actions perish; agency does not
quote: kāryatā kṣayiṇī tatra kartṛtvaṃ punar akṣayam
full: avasthāyugalaṃ cātra kāryakartṛtvaśabditam | kāryatā kṣayiṇī tatra kartṛtvaṃ punar akṣayam
words: condition of being effected / of being a product
agency, capacity of being an agent
proof: a- + kṣaya → akṣaya, neuter sg akṣayam
kāryatā with kṣayiṇī is feminine agreement
literal: The condition of being an effect is perishable; agency, however, is imperishable.
alternatives: Products cease; the fundamental capacity for agency is not exhausted by any particular deed.
judgement: The verse’s “agency” is a technical philosophical capacity, not a claim that an individual body can perform without limits or never die. Keep the antecedent “two conditions” from the first half in view.
recognition: Compare what comes and goes with the capacity from which actions issue. There is a deliberate shift from feminine kāryatā to neuter kartṛtvam; the agreement marks two distinct propositions.
exercise: Which adjective agrees with kāryatā, and which agrees with kartṛtvam?
answer: kṣayiṇī (f.nom.sg) qualifies kāryatā; akṣayam (n.nom.sg) qualifies kartṛtvam.
script_focus: कार्य contains र् + य, कर्तृत्व contains त् + ऋ and त् + व (different vowel/conjunct mechanisms).
why: The sharp distinction between a product and an agent is actually legible in Sanskrit morphology.
author: Kallaṭa / Vasugupta tradition; exact authorship debated
source_note: GRETIL + Mahānaya; do not assert sole authorship with certainty.

context_devanagari: अवस्थायुगलं चात्र कार्यकर्तृत्वशब्दितम् । कार्यता क्षयिणी तत्र कर्तृत्वं पुनर् अक्षयम् ॥

title: Power that is knowing and known
full: jñānajñeyasvarūpiṇyā śaktyā paramayā yutaḥ | padadvaye vibhur bhāti tadanyatra tu cinmayaḥ
words: having the forms of knowing and what is known
masculine nominative singular past passive participle
proof: jñāna + jñeya (√jñā + gerundive -ya) + svarūpin → jñānajñeyasvarūpin, feminine form svarūpiṇī
literal: Endowed with the supreme power whose forms are knowledge and the knowable…
alternatives: The Lord, joined with the highest Śakti that presents both cognition and its object…
judgement: This is **not a sentence by itself**: vibhur bhāti in the next half provides the subject and finite verb. Nor does instrumental śaktyā imply there are two absolutely independent realities.
recognition: The grammatical agreement among three feminine instrumentals shows a single descriptive complex. Philosophically, knowing and known appear as two aspects of one power.
exercise: Why do svarūpiṇyā, śaktyā and paramayā share case but have different internal endings?
answer: All are feminine instrumental singular. They follow different stem classes: -inī, -i, and -ā.
script_focus: ज्ञा = ज्+ञा; ज्ञेय has े; शक्ति uses क्त; स्वरूपिण्या combines ण्य + ा.
why: A precise capstone on feminine declensions, instrumental functions and the limits of extracting a single half-verse.
author: Kallaṭa / Vasugupta tradition; exact authorship debated
source_note: GRETIL + Mahānaya; do not assert sole authorship with certainty.
context_devanagari: ज्ञानज्ञेयस्वरूपिण्या शक्त्या परमया युतः । पदद्वये विभुर् भाति तदन्यत्र तु चिन्मयः ॥

title: How the infinite becomes the finite
quote: māyāparigrahavaśād bodho malinaḥ pumān paśur bhavati
full: māyāparigrahavaśād bodho malinaḥ pumān paśur bhavati | kālakalāniyatibalād rāgāvidyāvaśena saṃbaddhaḥ
words: because of coming under the sway of adopting Māyā
proof: bodhaḥ + malinaḥ → bodho malinaḥ (aḥ before m→o)
paśuḥ + bhavati → paśur bhavati (-uḥ→ur before voiced b)
√bhū present third singular gives bhavati, a present stem formation
literal: Through the sway of adopting Māyā, awareness, obscured, becomes the limited person, a bound subject.
alternatives: In taking on Māyā, knowing appears contracted as a finite experiencer—a paśu.
judgement: The subject chain is compressed and warrants discussion: bodhaḥ, pumān and paśuḥ are all nominatives, while malinaḥ qualifies the state of the subject. Avoid inventing three separate substances merely because English wants separate subjects.
recognition: We can now reconstruct the contraction argument without mythology. A causal ablative gives a condition; a finite verb names becoming; nominal forms identify what has become bound. Recognition will reverse mistaken identification without pretending individual embodiment was merely linguistic.
exercise: Explain the two ending changes vaśāt→vaśād and paśuḥ→paśur. What verb says “becomes”?
answer: Voicing of t before b; uḥ→ur before bh; bhavati is 3sg present active of √bhū.
script_focus: मायापरिग्रह has ग्रह conjunct; मलिनः ends in visarga; पुमान् a long-ā nominative; पशुर् has explicit r in sandhi.
why: All earlier morphology returns in a single powerful statement about limitation.
author: Abhinavagupta
source_note: GRETIL transliteration checked against SanskritDocuments where appropriate; commercial reuse of GRETIL transcription not cleared.

title: Bondage and freedom, read exactly
quote: etau bandhavimokṣau ca parameśasvarūpataḥ | na bhidyete na bhedo hi tattvataḥ parameśvare
full: etau bandhavimokṣau ca parameśasvarūpataḥ | na bhidyete na bhedo hi tattvataḥ parameśvare
words: from the standpoint of the Supreme Lord’s own nature
in reality, from the standpoint of truth
proof: √bhid passive present third dual → bhidyete (not 3rd plural bhidyante)
bhedaḥ + hi → bhedo hi (aḥ→o before h)
literal: These two—bondage and liberation—are not differentiated from the standpoint of the Supreme Lord’s own nature; for in ultimate reality there is no difference in the Lord.
alternatives: Viewed through the Lord’s essential being, bondage and release are not ultimately two separate realities.
judgement: **The standpoint is essential.** The verse is not asserting that a suffering bound subject experiences the same condition as one who has recognized freedom. Parameśasvarūpataḥ and tattvataḥ restrict the claim to the ultimate perspective.
recognition: Everything learned returns: dual number (etau, -au, bhidyete), nominal predicates (bhedaḥ), locative (parameśvare), two ablatival adverbs (-taḥ) and sandhi. Once the derivation is clear, the reader may decide how far the nondual claim reaches.
exercise: Determine whether bhidyete refers to one, two or many; explain why etau and bandhavimokṣau have matching -au endings.
answer: Third-person dual passive; etau and bandhavimokṣau are both masculine nominative dual. The two are bondage and liberation.
script_focus: एतौ and मोक्षौ share the औ sign; भिद्येते has द् + य and long e; तत्त्वतः uses त्त्व and final visarga.
why: The final lesson is a full verse, and the resolution comes from grammatical reconstruction, not faith in an English aphorism.
author: Abhinavagupta
source_note: Mahānaya + GRETIL transcription; punctuation, compounds and variant vowels still require printed-witness rights check.
